candidates.statement: Connect with colleagues and former classmates on LinkedIn to see what they are up to.
candidates.modality: present habitual practice ('some of the things that I do')

evidence_candidates.quote: networking just connecting with other colleagues, or maybe kind of past classmates see what they're up to

candidates.statement: Do a lot of marketing on LinkedIn because the exposure is far better than Google Ads, Facebook or other channels in the stakeholder's field.
candidates.modality: explicit present practice with comparison

evidence_candidates.quote: We do a lot of marketing especially in my field. We work with a lot of other professionals. In some areas, you know, marketing the exposure, there is far better than we might get, you know, through Google ads or Facebook out of other channels. So we focus a lot on marketing.

candidates.statement: Recruit through LinkedIn to source many people at a fairly low cost compared with competitors.
candidates.modality: explicit present practice

evidence_candidates.quote: We do a lot of recruiting as well through Linkedin. just good source a lot of people. And it's fairly low cost compared to some of the other competitors.

candidates.statement: Look for jobs for himself on LinkedIn and check what salary ranges are out there from time to time.
candidates.modality: hedged ('sometimes it's nice to kind of poke around')

evidence_candidates.quote: And then even looking for jobs for myself. Yeah, sometimes it's nice to kind of poke around. See what else is out there in the world, and just see what some of the salary ranges and things like that, you know, always keeps you motivated.

candidates.statement: Check community events posted on LinkedIn when he has the availability and bandwidth.
candidates.modality: conditional ('when I have the availability ... can have the bandwidth')
context: emails arrive in a firehose, so he cannot otherwise keep up

evidence_candidates.quote: I drink from the fire hose of emails and there's no chance that I would be able to otherwise keep up with everything. So it's nice that when I have the availability, and I think I, you know, can have the bandwidth. I can go on and check and see kind of what events are, you know, being put on the community.

candidates.statement: Signal to clients that he exists, with credentials and degrees, so the profile lends credibility.
candidates.modality: explicit purpose statement ('mostly to just signal')

evidence_candidates.quote: It's mostly to just signal to like my other to my clients, for example, that I I. You know I exist. I'm a person who, you know, has credentials, and I have, you know, degrees, and it just lends a little bit of a you know. a bit of credibility.

candidates.statement: Keep LinkedIn as a place where people can verify he is who he says he is and not a scammer, including a matching photo.
candidates.modality: explicit ('another resource for people to check in')

evidence_candidates.quote: It's more of just a you know, another resource for people to check in and just make sure. Okay, I'm not like a Scammer. I'm not a, you know. If they get an email from me I am who I say I am, and the picture there matches the picture that they see on, you know, Zoom, or or you know, when I meet in person.

candidates.statement: LinkedIn contributes to his overall professional development.
candidates.modality: denied ('I can't say it's actually played that much of a role')

evidence_candidates.quote: So for my own professional development. I can't say it's actually played that much of a role.

candidates.statement: Marketing resources are good but LinkedIn charges a lot, so cost is a consideration.
candidates.modality: evaluative comment on pricing ('cost is definitely a consideration')

evidence_candidates.quote: I mean, they do charge you an arm and a leg. So I think cost is definitely a consideration there.

candidates.statement: Use LinkedIn's easy, user-friendly posting tools so that broad-based marketing can be targeted.
candidates.modality: positive evaluation of feature usefulness ('very, very easy and user friendly')

evidence_candidates.quote: some of the tools that they have to like post you know, marketing things are are very, very easy and user friendly. So kind of makes it again, a good tool for any sort of broad based marketing you can get, you know, pretty targeted.

candidates.statement: Pay to have posts recommended more, and keep track of impressions and marketing metrics.
candidates.modality: second-person capability description ('you can pay', 'you can kind of keep track')

evidence_candidates.quote: They have like recommendations. You can pay to have it be recommended a little bit more. And that process is just really simple. They just tell you here's how much it's gonna cost. And you know, here's how much it's gonna get boosted. So you can kind of keep track of all your impressions and all of your different marketing metrics.

candidates.statement: Use the acquired e-learning platform (Lynda/LinkedIn Learning) for a quick deep dive into a technology stack or marketing practice, because its quality exceeds YouTube.
candidates.modality: past positive evaluation ('I did like', 'one of the better places to go')

evidence_candidates.quote: If you want to do kind of a quick, deep dive into a certain. You know technology stack, or you want to kind of get a better understanding of like, how do I, you know, do something in marketing a little bit better. that was actually one of the better places to go, because in terms of quality it would definitely exceed. You know what you might find on Youtube or some of those other resources.

candidates.statement: Post something about what is happening at a conference as a marketing/awareness post.
candidates.modality: typical practice ('Typically what we'll do')
context: when something interesting is happening at a conference

evidence_candidates.quote: So let's say, I'm at a conference. And yeah, something interesting is happening. Typically what we'll do is yeah, post something about it.

candidates.statement: Schedule the post for 9 AM the next morning when people first show up at the office instead of posting in the evening, to get more impressions.
candidates.modality: explicit intention ('So I'm going to be posted at ... 9 Am. Tomorrow')

evidence_candidates.quote: it doesn't really make sense, you know, in the evening, to post it. It's just not going to get as many impressions. So I'm going to be posted at, you know. 9 Am. Tomorrow, when people 1st show up at the office, and I'll get a nice kind of boost in some of the impressions.

candidates.statement: Get interactions once the post is on the feed and hopefully eventually win some business.
candidates.modality: expected then hedged hope ('hopefully, eventually')

evidence_candidates.quote: So once I've posted it, it goes out to the network and it's on the feed, so I'll start to kind of get some interactions. And you know. hopefully, eventually win some business.

candidates.statement: Research a prospect's profile and background for common threads before adding them; do not do cold calls or cold adds.
candidates.modality: conditional practice plus explicit negative ('I don't reach out too much as kind of cold call or cold')

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe I'll search for their name if there's somebody that I'm you know, interested in learning more about. Maybe they're a C, you know, c-suite at a company that we're looking to sell to. I want to get a little background on them, I'll you know, search them in the search function, pull up their profile, kind of take a quick look at their background to see if there's any kind of common threads, and then maybe I'll you know I'll add them.

I don't often kind of reach out and connect with you know other folks. It's like more. If it's somebody I know, I'll reach out and add them but I don't reach out too much as kind of cold call or cold.

candidates.statement: Use LinkedIn about 4 out of 5 days a week in some way, shape or form.
candidates.modality: factual frequency report

evidence_candidates.quote: let's call it 4 out of 5 days a week I'm on Linkedin in some way, shape or form.

candidates.statement: For recruiting in the small Laravel community, posting on Lara Jobs yields better candidates than posting on LinkedIn.
candidates.modality: comparative factual report

evidence_candidates.quote: for example, recruiting like the Laravel community is pretty small. And you know, Lara jobs. If you post something there, you actually get better candidates than you might get from yeah posting something on Linkedin.

candidates.statement: The amount of ads and targeted content plus the cluttered interface cloud the feed with irrelevant noise; he does not care for it.
candidates.modality: frustration report ('would probably be the biggest frustration')
context: when he is on LinkedIn with a mission, e.g. to post something

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes the amount of ads and the amount of you know targeted stuff feels a little much. It just kind of clouds your feed, and there's a lot of irrelevant stuff there.

And then certain parts of the interface. our just too cluttered. I think they throw a lot of information just to make it very busy. They want you click it everywhere. But in certain cases, yeah, I'm there for a reason. I have a mission. I gotta post something. I want to turn that into, you know impressions, and having that, all of this other stuff is kind of just added noise. And I yeah, don't necessarily care for it.

candidates.statement: LinkedIn's core has not evolved much; it has focused on more targeted marketing tools and acquired the e-learning platform.
candidates.modality: observation about platform evolution

evidence_candidates.quote: I mean its core hasn't evolved much for the most part, you know, since it was acquired by Microsoft, it hasn't changed a great deal.

candidates.statement: New AI tools that help develop content for posts are new and interesting.
candidates.modality: interest observation ('pretty new and interesting')

evidence_candidates.quote: there's some new like AI tools to help with developing content for posts. Yeah, that's pretty new and interesting.

candidates.statement: Have LinkedIn provide support for content development, with more of it automated, so that a smaller marketing team is needed.
candidates.modality: suggestion ('would be great to have more of that kind of automated')

evidence_candidates.quote: Probably the biggest would just be, you know, support for content development, and then, you know, would be great to have more of that kind of automated. So we don't have to have as big of a marketing team, or that's always a pain

candidates.statement: Be able to post professional-looking content without being reviewed six times or going through the whole marketing funnel.
candidates.modality: suggestion ('it'd be great to be able to')
context: design is at a premium and takes a while

evidence_candidates.quote: Design is at a premium, and that just always takes a while. So it'd be great to be able to post, you know, professional looking stuff without having to be, you know, reviewed 6 times, and go through kind of the whole marketing funnel.

candidates.statement: Adding a feature that cuts down the time would be a really good feature to add.
candidates.modality: interviewer endorsement

evidence_candidates.quote: Yes, yes, that would be a really good feature to add right? It really cut cuts down the time.

candidates.statement: LinkedIn is mostly a professional networking platform that lets professionals connect and live in the business world.
candidates.modality: general description of the platform

evidence_candidates.quote: So Linkedin is, I mean, in my view, is mostly a kind of networking platform. There's kind of a couple of key things that I do on it. But by and large it's, you know, viewed as a professional networking platform, which is, you know. in parallel to a lot of the other social media. It exists out there just to allow kind of professionals to connect and you know, live in the business world.
